# iotsa board reference

Every board iotsa knows about, generated from the single source of truth
[`iotsa-board.json`](../iotsa-board.json). The build sections in
`iotsa-board-defs.ini` (and each example's `platformio.ini`) come from the same
file. Processor/USB-wiring *traits* are one layer down, hand-authored in
[`iotsa-board-traits.ini`](../iotsa-board-traits.ini).

## At a glance

| Board | Chip | Status | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`iotsa_v4`](#iotsa_v4) | ESP8266 (ESP-12) | supported | iotsa's own custom PCB: ESP-12 module, FTDI programming header. The reference ESP8266 target. |
| [`esp32thing`](#esp32thing) | ESP32 (Xtensa dual-core) | supported | Historic default ESP32 board: lots of I/O, onboard LiPo charger. Now overpriced and physically large. |
| [`esp32dev`](#esp32dev) | ESP32 (Xtensa dual-core) | supported | Generic ESP32 devkit, usually a cheap clone. No LiPo charger. |
| [`lolin32`](#lolin32) | ESP32 (Xtensa dual-core) | supported | Compact ESP32 with an onboard TP4054 LiPo charger and JST-PH battery connector. |
| [`lolin32_oled`](#lolin32_oled) | ESP32 (Xtensa dual-core) | supported | ESP32 with a built-in 0.96" 128x64 SSD1306 wired to GPIO5 (SDA) / GPIO4 (SCL). No LiPo charger. |
| [`pico32`](#pico32) | ESP32-PICO-D4 (Xtensa dual-core SiP) | supported | Small ESP32-PICO board: enough pins, cheap. No LiPo charger. |
| [`esp32c3devkit`](#esp32c3devkit) | ESP32-C3 (RISC-V single-core) | supported | Reference ESP32-C3 devkit, external USB-serial chip. |
| [`esp32c3lcd`](#esp32c3lcd) | ESP32-C3 (RISC-V single-core) | experimental | ESP32-C3 with an attached LCD and only 2 MB flash. |
| [`esp32c3supermini`](#esp32c3supermini) | ESP32-C3 (RISC-V single-core) | supported | Tiny cheap ESP32-C3 board, native USB-Serial/JTAG, 4 MB flash. |
| [`crowpanel128`](#crowpanel128) | ESP32-C3 (RISC-V single-core) | supported | ESP32-C3 with a built-in 1.28" round IPS LCD (GC9A01). |
| [`esp32s3supermini`](#esp32s3supermini) | ESP32-S3 (Xtensa dual-core) + 2 MB PSRAM | supported | Tiny cheap ESP32-S3 board, native USB-Serial/JTAG, 4 MB flash + 2 MB PSRAM. |

## Boards

### <a id="iotsa_v4"></a>`iotsa_v4` — iotsa v4 board

iotsa's own custom PCB: ESP-12 module, FTDI programming header. The reference ESP8266 target.

- **Chip:** ESP8266 (ESP-12)
- **Status:** supported
- **PlatformIO board:** `nodemcuv2` · **Arduino FQBN:** `esp8266:esp8266:nodemcuv2`
- **Provenance:** iotsa-custom PCB
- **Constraints:** No BLE. HTTPS unreliable on ESP8266 (see cwi-dis/iotsa#159).
- **Reference:** `README.md#supported-hardware-variants`
- **Example:** examples/Skeleton (built as vanilla_esp8266)
- **Notes:** The canonical ESP8266 target; the vanilla_esp8266 alias points here.

### <a id="esp32thing"></a>`esp32thing` — SparkFun ESP32 Thing

Historic default ESP32 board: lots of I/O, onboard LiPo charger. Now overpriced and physically large.

- **Chip:** ESP32 (Xtensa dual-core)
- **Status:** supported
- **PlatformIO board:** `esp32thing` · **Arduino FQBN:** `esp32:esp32:esp32thing`
- **Provenance:** off-the-shelf
- **Reference:** [https://www.sparkfun.com/products/13907](https://www.sparkfun.com/products/13907)
- **Example:** sandbox/BLEClient
- **Notes:** Canonical vanilla_esp32 target for CI. Being phased out for esp32dev / pico32 / lolin32(_lite).

### <a id="esp32dev"></a>`esp32dev` — Espressif ESP32-DevKitC (or clone)

Generic ESP32 devkit, usually a cheap clone. No LiPo charger.

- **Chip:** ESP32 (Xtensa dual-core)
- **Status:** supported
- **PlatformIO board:** `esp32dev` · **Arduino FQBN:** `—`
- **Provenance:** off-the-shelf
- **Reference:** [https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32/hw-reference/esp32/get-started-devkitc.html](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32/hw-reference/esp32/get-started-devkitc.html)
- **Example:** sandbox/BLEClient
- **Notes:** Known to work, not continuously CI-tested. Current pick when no charger is needed.

### <a id="lolin32"></a>`lolin32` — WEMOS LOLIN32 Lite

Compact ESP32 with an onboard TP4054 LiPo charger and JST-PH battery connector.

- **Chip:** ESP32 (Xtensa dual-core)
- **Status:** supported
- **PlatformIO board:** `lolin32_lite` · **Arduino FQBN:** `esp32:esp32:lolin32-lite`
- **Build:** partitions `min_spiffs.csv`
- **Provenance:** off-the-shelf; key name is historical (the full LOLIN32 is not used, pio_board is the Lite -- cwi-dis/iotsa#228)
- **Constraints:** Fewer GPIOs broken out than a full devkit.
- **Reference:** [https://www.espboards.dev/esp32/lolin32-lite/](https://www.espboards.dev/esp32/lolin32-lite/)
- **Example:** sandbox/BLEClient
- **Notes:** The 'lolin32' key is kept (not renamed to lolin32_lite) so downstream `extends = lolin32` keeps resolving. Current pick when a LiPo charger is wanted.

### <a id="lolin32_oled"></a>`lolin32_oled` — WEMOS LOLIN32 OLED

ESP32 with a built-in 0.96" 128x64 SSD1306 wired to GPIO5 (SDA) / GPIO4 (SCL). No LiPo charger.

- **Chip:** ESP32 (Xtensa dual-core)
- **Status:** supported
- **PlatformIO board:** `lolin32_lite` · **Arduino FQBN:** `esp32:esp32:lolin32-lite`
- **Build:** partitions `min_spiffs.csv`
- **Provenance:** no PlatformIO/Arduino profile of its own; builds as lolin32_lite
- **Constraints:** Built-in OLED occupies GPIO5/GPIO4; fewer GPIOs broken out; no charger.
- **Reference:** [https://randomnerdtutorials.com/esp32-built-in-oled-ssd1306/](https://randomnerdtutorials.com/esp32-built-in-oled-ssd1306/)
- **Example:** cwi-dis/lissabon:lissabonController
- **Notes:** Added in cwi-dis/iotsa#229. lolin32_lite is used because its LED_BUILTIN=GPIO22 does not clash with the OLED's SDA on GPIO5 (the full lolin32 profile's GPIO5 would).

### <a id="pico32"></a>`pico32` — Espressif ESP32-PICO-KIT

Small ESP32-PICO board: enough pins, cheap. No LiPo charger.

- **Chip:** ESP32-PICO-D4 (Xtensa dual-core SiP)
- **Status:** supported
- **PlatformIO board:** `pico32` · **Arduino FQBN:** `—`
- **Provenance:** off-the-shelf
- **Constraints:** Minimodule JTAG debugging shares pins with the touchpads.
- **Reference:** [https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32/hw-reference/esp32/get-started-pico-kit.html](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32/hw-reference/esp32/get-started-pico-kit.html)
- **Example:** cwi-dis/lissabon:lissabonLedstrip
- **Notes:** Used by the lissabon ledstrip appliances.

### <a id="esp32c3devkit"></a>`esp32c3devkit` — Espressif ESP32-C3-DevKitM-1

Reference ESP32-C3 devkit, external USB-serial chip.

- **Chip:** ESP32-C3 (RISC-V single-core)
- **Status:** supported
- **PlatformIO board:** `esp32-c3-devkitm-1` · **Arduino FQBN:** `—`
- **Build:** build flags `-DIOTSA_PIN_NEOPIXEL=8`
- **Provenance:** off-the-shelf
- **Constraints:** No PCNT (no rotary encoder), no touch, no analog voltage reading, no deep-sleep wakeup. Reduced WiFi TX power defaults on.
- **Reference:** [https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32c3/hw-reference/esp32c3/user-guide-devkitm-1.html](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32c3/hw-reference/esp32c3/user-guide-devkitm-1.html)
- **Example:** examples/Led (built as vanilla_esp32c3)
- **Notes:** Canonical vanilla_esp32c3 target for CI.

### <a id="esp32c3lcd"></a>`esp32c3lcd` — ESP32-C3 board with LCD (2 MB)

ESP32-C3 with an attached LCD and only 2 MB flash.

- **Chip:** ESP32-C3 (RISC-V single-core)
- **Status:** experimental
- **PlatformIO board:** `esp32-c3-devkitm-1` · **Arduino FQBN:** `—`
- **Build:** partitions `bare_minimum_2MB.csv`, flash 2MB
- **Provenance:** off-the-shelf; native USB CDC
- **Constraints:** 2 MB flash: bare_minimum_2MB.csv partitions, extremely tight. Plus all ESP32-C3 limits.
- **Reference:** —
- **Example:** —
- **Notes:** Barely fits a full-featured app; no iotsa example or downstream user yet.

### <a id="esp32c3supermini"></a>`esp32c3supermini` — ESP32-C3 SuperMini (clone)

Tiny cheap ESP32-C3 board, native USB-Serial/JTAG, 4 MB flash.

- **Chip:** ESP32-C3 (RISC-V single-core)
- **Status:** supported
- **PlatformIO board:** `esp32-c3-devkitm-1` · **Arduino FQBN:** `—`
- **Build:** partitions `min_spiffs.csv`, flash 4MB
- **Provenance:** off-the-shelf clone
- **Constraints:** All ESP32-C3 limits (no PCNT / touch / analog Vbat / deep-sleep wakeup).
- **Reference:** [https://www.espboards.dev/esp32/esp32-c3-super-mini/](https://www.espboards.dev/esp32/esp32-c3-super-mini/)
- **Example:** examples/DateTime
- **Notes:** The in-progress P1-port-powered iotsaSmartMeter build targets this (cwi-dis/iotsaSmartMeter#1).

### <a id="crowpanel128"></a>`crowpanel128` — Elecrow CrowPanel 1.28" round LCD

ESP32-C3 with a built-in 1.28" round IPS LCD (GC9A01).

- **Chip:** ESP32-C3 (RISC-V single-core)
- **Status:** supported
- **PlatformIO board:** `esp32-c3-devkitm-1` · **Arduino FQBN:** `—`
- **Build:** partitions `min_spiffs.csv`, flash 4MB
- **Provenance:** off-the-shelf; external USB-serial
- **Constraints:** min_spiffs.csv required -- a full C3 app (LovyanGFX + HTTPS) overflows default.csv (cwi-dis/iotsa#226). Plus all ESP32-C3 limits.
- **Reference:** [https://www.elecrow.com/crowpanel-esp32-1-28-inch-240x240-hd-ips-round-display.html](https://www.elecrow.com/crowpanel-esp32-1-28-inch-240x240-hd-ips-round-display.html)
- **Example:** cwi-dis/iotsaNeoClock:crowpanel128
- **Notes:** Used by iotsaNeoClock's round-LCD clock. Partitions fixed in cwi-dis/iotsa#226.

### <a id="esp32s3supermini"></a>`esp32s3supermini` — ESP32-S3 SuperMini (clone)

Tiny cheap ESP32-S3 board, native USB-Serial/JTAG, 4 MB flash + 2 MB PSRAM.

- **Chip:** ESP32-S3 (Xtensa dual-core) + 2 MB PSRAM
- **Status:** supported
- **PlatformIO board:** `esp32-s3-devkitc-1` · **Arduino FQBN:** `esp32:esp32:esp32s3`
- **Build:** partitions `min_spiffs.csv`, flash 4MB, build flags `-DIOTSA_PIN_NEOPIXEL=48`
- **Provenance:** off-the-shelf clone
- **Constraints:** Clone boards run hot; intermittent WiFi drops even with wifiPowerReduction (cwi-dis/iotsa#194). USB-OTG/TinyUSB not implemented.
- **Reference:** [https://www.espboards.dev/esp32/esp32-s3-super-mini/](https://www.espboards.dev/esp32/esp32-s3-super-mini/)
- **Example:** sandbox/BLEClient (built as vanilla_esp32s3)
- **Notes:** BLE confirmed working, including BLE/HPS-only (no WiFi) operation.

## Role aliases

Build targets that mean "whichever real board is iotsa's current default for
this chip family" -- examples and tests target these, not a concrete board.

| Alias | Currently | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `vanilla_esp8266` | [`iotsa_v4`](#iotsa_v4) | iotsa's current default plain ESP8266 target. |
| `vanilla_esp32` | [`esp32thing`](#esp32thing) | iotsa's current default plain ESP32 target. |
| `vanilla_esp32c3` | [`esp32c3devkit`](#esp32c3devkit) | iotsa's current default plain ESP32-C3 target. |
| `vanilla_esp32s3` | [`esp32s3supermini`](#esp32s3supermini) | iotsa's current default plain ESP32-S3 target. |
